title: Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering
text:
Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse's mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.
 
 
**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering, you will lead process engineering. This role is part of the LEU+ Manufacturing Program, a capital expansion of Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility. The program aims to manufacture LEU+ (higher-enrichment low-enriched uranium) nuclear fuel. Accountable for the design, qualification and startup of the new manufacturing processes, including uranium conversion, pellet production, fuel rod and assembly manufacturing, uranium recovery and recycling, and the laboratory and maintenance areas. Plan and direct the methods, equipment and processes needed to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective fuel, and develops the engineers who deliver them.
 
 
You will report to the Project Director, LEU+ Manufacturing Program and be located at Columbia, SC. You will support this role 100% onsite.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the LEU+ Process Engineering organization with responsibility for safety, regulatory compliance, product quality, technical execution, cost, schedule, and operational readiness.
* Lead process engineering activities supporting nuclear safety, including Integrated Safety Analysis, hazard analysis, IROFS, criticality safety, NRC licensing activities, and regulatory change control.
* Oversee process engineering deliverables from initial design through equipment procurement, installation, commissioning, qualification, startup, and turnover to Operations.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment and processes meet product quality, nuclear safety, performance, and qualification requirements.
* Lead mechanical, chemical, and process engineering resources while forecasting staffing needs and assigning technical ownership.
* Coordinate technical interfaces across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, Construction, Commissioning, Automation/IT, and suppliers.
* Manage process engineering scope, budget, schedule, risks, and change control while providing clear status reporting to program leadership.
* Guide manufacturing optimization using Lean/Six Sigma, OEE, capacity analysis, bottleneck reduction, and continuous improvement.
* Support operational readiness through procedures, training, spare-parts planning, startup support, and turnover of qualified manufacturing processes.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in process engineering, manufacturing, plant operations, capital projects, or related technical leadership.
* 5+ years of people-management experience leading engineers and managing technical resources and budgets.
* Demonstrated leadership of complex, diverse engineering or manufacturing programs with accountability for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and technical performance.
* Knowledge of process engineering, process safety, hazard analysis, manufacturing systems, and equipment/process qualification.
* Experience managing complex capital projects from design through commissioning, qualification, and operational readiness.
* Experience in nuclear fuel, nuclear materials, chemical processing, or a similarly regulated manufacturing environment.
* Knowledge of 10 CFR Part 70, Integrated Safety Analysis, nuclear safety controls, and regulatory change control.
* Knowledge of nuclear fuel manufacturing processes, including conversion, pelleting, rod/assembly manufacturing, or uranium recovery, preferred.
* Demonstrated experience with project controls, resource planning, budgeting, risk management, and change control.
* Experience developing leaders, building technical teams, and influencing across functional and organizational boundaries.
* Experience delivering continuous improvement and financial results without compromising safety, quality, or regulatory compliance.
* Lean Six Sigma experience required

We are committed to transparency and equity in all of our people practices. The base salary range for this position, which is dependent upon experience, qualifications and skills, is estimated to be $144,000 to $180,000 per year.
 
 
**Why Westinghouse?**
**Benefits**
**Our benefits package is tailored to meet the diverse needs of our employees, while also promoting wellness and career growth. The following are representative of what we offer:**

* Comprehensive Medical benefits which could include medical, dental, vision, prescription coverage and Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contributions options
* Wellness Programs designed to support employees in maintaining their health and well-being including Employee Assistance Program providing support for our employees and their household members
* 401(k) with Company Match Contributions to support employees' retirement
* Paid Vacations and Company Holidays
* Opportunities for Flexible Work Arrangements to promote work-life balance
* Educational Reimbursement and Comprehensive Career Programs to help employees grow in their careers
* Global Recognition and Service Programs to celebrate employee accomplishments and service
* Employee Referral Program

Westinghouse Electric Company Is The Global Nuclear Energy Industry's First Choice For Safe, Clean, And Efficient Energy Solutions. We Enable Our Delivery Of This Vision By Living Our Value System
 
 

* Safety and Quality
* Integrity and Trust
* Customer Focus and Innovation
* Speed and Passion to Win
* Teamwork and Accountability
